name: International Protection (UNHCR Mandate RSD via Immigration Act, No Dedicated Legislation)

requirements.blocker_text: Must establish a well-founded fear of persecution to UNHCR, which conducts all refugee status determination under its mandate; cases are typically identified and channelled through Living Water Community, UNHCR's local implementing partner NGO.

evidence_required.document: Personal account/testimony at UNHCR RSD interview

sources.title: UNHCR Trinidad and Tobago -- International Protection in Trinidad and Tobago: no dedicated refugee legislation (operates under the 1976 Immigration Act), T&T acceded to the 1951 Refugee Convention/1967 Protocol in November 2000, UNHCR conducts all RSD under mandate, Living Water Community as identification/referral partner, unimplemented 2014 'phased approach' policy

Refugees International -- Forced into Illegality: Venezuelan Refugees and Migrants in Trinidad and Tobago: even UNHCR-recognised refugees receive only non-deportation, free movement, and family reunification -- explicitly NOT legal work rights or other services; ~440 detained as of November 2018; some recognised refugees reportedly charged with illegal entry despite protected status; 2014 policy never implemented

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Trinidad and Tobago's initial build. Built (rather than excluded) because, unlike Curacao and Aruba earlier this session, Trinidad and Tobago DOES have a real, tier-1/tier-2-confirmed recognition pathway: it is a 1951 Convention party, UNHCR conducts full mandate refugee status determination here (unlike the smaller BOTs, where UNHCR's role is often described more thinly), and a partner NGO (Living Water Community) actively identifies and refers cases -- and recognition DOES confer defined legal rights (non-deportation, free movement, family reunification), even though those rights conspicuously exclude the right to work or access other services. outcome fields reflect that narrow reality: work_rights and study_rights are 'none' (explicitly excluded per the Refugees International report) while family_can_join is modelled as true (family reunification IS one of the three rights recognised refugees receive) -- a more granular, evidence-based outcome than a blanket none/false across the board. STATUS: DRAFT because sourcing is tier-2 throughout (UNHCR and an NGO/think-tank report, not a T&T government page) and because the same Refugees International report documents serious implementation gaps: the government's own 2014 policy commitment to build 'comprehensive national capacity' for refugee matters remains unimplemented over a decade later, hundreds have been held in immigration detention, and the report specifically states some UNHCR-recognised refugees have been charged with illegal entry despite their protected status -- meaning the status this route describes is real on paper but has documented, serious gaps between recognition and actual treatment in practice. This is a middle case between Cayman's (codified and enforced, built as draft) and Curacao/Aruba's (no functioning protection at all, excluded and disclosed only) -- flagged explicitly as such rather than forced into either bucket.
